description: JD-driven tutorial suggestion, extraction (75-band). Turn the canonical JD document ingested in 74 into a structured list of required skills / tools / competencies via a model-backed pass, built in the curriculum_gen.py HOUSE STYLE: ask for JSON, extract it forgivingly (extract_json), then validate strictly before anything downstream trusts it (subject_from_dict is the model to follow — lenient about what the model omits, strict about what would break the consumer). This is the one model-backed step of the JD funnel; it reuses the BYO-key LLM client (praxis/llm.py, agora optional) that band 20 introduced. Depends on 74 (there must be a canonical JD to extract from). Anti-fabrication: a requirement list is only produced when the model's JSON validates against the strict schema; a payload that omits required fields or invents an unusable shape is rejected and repaired with the grader's own sentences, never silently coerced into a downstream call.
warmup: echo '--- the house style: ask JSON, extract forgivingly, validate strictly ---'; sed -n '45,150p' praxis/curriculum_gen.py
echo '--- the strict validator to mirror ---'; sed -n '561,623p' curriculum.py
echo '--- the shared LLM client (BYO-key, agora optional) ---'; grep -n 'class \|def ask\|AGORA_BASE_URL\|def complete' praxis/llm.py | head

userStories.title: Model-backed extraction of a JD into structured requirements
acceptanceCriteria: A new extraction module in the construction core (e.g. praxis/jd_extract.py) takes the canonical JD from 74 and, via the band-20 LLM client, asks the model for a JSON list of required skills / tools / competencies, each item carrying at least a normalized name and a kind (skill / tool / competency) plus the JD span or phrase it came from.

It reuses the curriculum_gen.py house style exactly: a build_prompt-style prompt that pins the JSON shape verbatim, an extract_json-style forgiving parse (fenced or bare JSON), then a strict normalize+validate step modeled on subject_from_dict — lenient about omitted optional fields, strict about anything a downstream band would choke on.
The extraction runs only on the model-backed path (needs a key / 503 when none, like construct's short-answer grading); no requirement is invented locally.
Gate green: python3 -m pytest -q tests/ passes, including a test that runs extraction against a mocked LLM reply (fenced + bare JSON variants) and asserts a well-formed, normalized requirement list.
userStories.notes: python3 -m pytest -q tests/: 871 passed, 0 failed (10 new in tests/test_jd_extract.py, fenced + bare JSON variants both normalize to the same 5-requirement list)

userStories.title: Strict validation rejects and repairs an unusable payload
acceptanceCriteria: The validator rejects a model payload that omits a required field or returns a shape the gap-analysis band (76) could not consume, raising a specific, actionable error (the sentences double as the eventual UI error text, per the construct.py _repair_prompt pattern).

A rejected payload is fed back to the model with the validator's own sentences for one repair attempt rather than retried blind, and a still-invalid result is surfaced as a failure — never coerced into a partial list.

Gate green: python3 -m pytest -q tests/ covers at least one malformed-payload case (missing field / wrong type) asserting it is rejected with the actionable message, and one repair case asserting the second attempt is accepted.
userStories.notes: python3 -m pytest -q tests/: 885 passed, 0 failed (14 new; tests/test_jd_extract.py 24 passed). A rejected payload triggers exactly one repair carrying the validator's sentences + the draft (2 calls asserted), and a still-invalid second attempt raises with all failures and no partial list.
